findings.description: No code writes a `landed` event. So every session merged with `pup merge --pr` stays in "Needs you" and in the fleet view forever, even after its PR is merged or closed on GitHub, and the operator has no way to clear it.
findings.body:
**A `pr-open` inbox entry can never be cleared.**

`openPullRequest` treats a merged session's PR as open until a `landed` event follows it. Nothing in `src/` writes `landed`: the only references are this reader, its doc comments, and a test that inserts the row with raw SQL (`dashboard.test.ts`). Decision 83 says "Nothing writes `landed` yet; `pup land` will", but it doesn't say what follows from that.

```ts
function openPullRequest(newestFirst: EventRow[]): string | undefined {
  for (const row of newestFirst) {
    const type: string = row.type;
    if (type === 'landed') return undefined;
    ...
    return event.prUrl === undefined ? undefined : sanitizeReason(event.prUrl) || undefined;
```

What follows:
- **Nothing clears an entry.** `merged` is a terminal state (`session-state.utils.ts:37`) and no code prunes sessions. So `needOf` returns `pr-open` for that session for as long as its row exists. That holds whether the PR was merged on GitHub, closed, or left open.
- **Every conductor merge adds one.** The conductor may only use `pup merge --pr` (`profile-compiler.service.ts:571-576`), and `merge-gate.service.ts:1113-1119` stores `prUrl` on each of those merges.
- **Old stores flood on upgrade.** Every `--pr` session a project ever ran appears at once as `PR opened, not landed → <url>`. That puts back, at the top of the output, the "stayed on it for good" clutter decision 83 sets out to remove.
- **The fleet view regresses.** `fleetSummary.needsYou` now folds from `needsYou(snapshot)` (L133). `fleetBlockLines` (`src/cli/ui/dashboard-text.utils.ts:163`) prints each entry with `sessionLine`, so every registered project now shows bare `merged <id> <branch>` rows with no reason.
- **The conductor is misinformed.** It reads `pup status` on every step and is told permanently that this finished work is waiting.

Possible fixes:
- Hold back the `pr-open` kind until a `landed` writer exists.
- Or check the PR's real state through the adapter layer.
- Or, at minimum, keep `pr-open` out of `fleetSummary` and record the limitation in decision 83.

findings.description: `stallReason` copies the `STALLED (...)` and `TURN DIED (API error) — ...` wording from `activityLabel`/`deadTurnLabel` in src/cli/ui/dashboard-text.utils.ts instead of sharing it. Its JSDoc promises the inbox and the table "never describe one stall two ways" (decision 52), but only a test keeps the two copies in step. Moving the stall wording next to `formatStaleAge` in src/core would let both call one function.

The fleet view now lists question and open-PR sessions, but prints them with `sessionLine`, which shows neither the question nor the PR url. A merged row reads only `merged <id> <branch>` and doesn't say why it needs the operator.

`openPullRequest` scrubs control characters from the stored prUrl but doesn't check that it is an http(s) URL, as `safeHttpUrl` in session-dossier.service.ts does. A tampered merge event could therefore put any one-line command text in the inbox's "answer" slot, which the conductor reads. This is defence in depth only: it needs a store write, which decisions 46 and 57 already accept.

The CLI decides which states count as finished (`s.state !== 'merged' && s.state !== 'killed'`) inline. That classification belongs in src/core next to `fleetSummary`, which already counts merged and killed, so src/cli stays thin.
The edited `fleetSummary` JSDoc now mixes the new inbox set ("Awaiting review is there…") with the old fleet-summary wording about awaiting-input, so it no longer describes a single set clearly.

Decision 83's "says `Nothing running and nothing planned.` again" is loose: that line was never removed. The decision also doesn't mention that an open-PR inbox line can print directly above it, because the merged row is hidden from the table but still listed in the inbox.
